headline: Your tools are leveling up
subheadline: Figma gets ChatGPT Images 2.0, Cursor ships parallel agents, and Claude Code gets faster sessions — all directly impacting your MCP + design system work.

sections.label: Trending
sections.title: Figma adds ChatGPT Images 2.0 across Design, Draw, Slides, and Weave
sections.description: OpenAI's newest image model is now baked into Make Image and Edit Image across virtually every Figma surface — Design, Draw, Slides, Buzz, FigJam, and Weave. For your white-label sport apps, this could mean rapid asset generation and visual exploration without leaving Figma. Worth testing how it handles brand-constrained imagery.

sections.label: Read
sections.title: Figma MCP server now generates design layers from VS Code
sections.description: The Figma MCP server can now push rendered UI back into Figma as editable frames — not just pull design context into code. This is a big deal for your MCP + Claude integration work. It means the loop is closing: AI generates code, code renders, rendered output lands back in Figma as real layers. Two-way bridge, not one-way street.

sections.label: Read
sections.title: Claude Code ships faster startup, better MCP startup, and session resume
sections.description: Claude Code's April release focuses on exactly the friction points you'd hit in longer design system sessions — quicker MCP startup, better session resume so you don't lose context, and improved plugin management. If your Figma MCP + Claude workflows have felt sluggish on big files, this update is worth pulling.

sections.label: Try this tool
sections.title: Cursor's new tiled Agents Window — run multiple agents in parallel
sections.description: Cursor's latest update lets you run multiple agents side-by-side in a tiled layout, with branch selection from empty state and file search filters for scoping. Think: one agent refactoring your component tokens while another generates a new variant. If you're vibe-coding with Cursor, this is a workflow multiplier.

sections.label: Concept of the day
sections.title: Design systems as dynamic infrastructure, not static component libraries
sections.description: The framing here is sharp: in 2026, design systems at Airbnb and Uber have shifted from static component libraries to data-driven infrastructure that feeds both human interfaces AND AI agents. This is exactly the trajectory your white-label sport app system should be on — tokens and components that aren't just consumed by designers, but queryable by Claude via MCP.

sections.label: Read
sections.title: Figma's AI Feature Spec Generator — describe features, get user flows and edge cases
sections.description: Figma Make now takes plain-language feature descriptions and maps them into user flows, states, logic, and edge cases — then lets you prototype and inspect code without leaving Figma. For someone who thinks at the product/strategy level, this could collapse the gap between your product thinking and actual spec handoff dramatically.

sections.label: Think about this
sections.title: If your design system is AI-queryable, does the designer's role shift from maker to curator?
sections.description: With Figma MCP enabling two-way flow between code and design, and Claude Code getting faster at understanding component systems — the person who architects what the AI can access and generate becomes more powerful than the person who pushes pixels. Your MCP integration work isn't just a technical project. It's positioning you for what design leadership looks like next.
